prompt: `note` holds the string `bold?`, and the template writes `{{ note }}`. What does the page show?

choices.text: The word `bold?` in bold
choices.why: That would mean the string became markup, which interpolation never lets happen.

choices.text: The characters `bold?`, as text
choices.why: Right. Interpolation always produces text.

choices.text: Nothing, because Angular removes HTML from strings
choices.why: Nothing is removed; the characters are shown as they are.

choices.text: A build error, because the string looks like a tag
choices.why: The compiler does not inspect the contents of a string field.

prompt: Which of these may a template expression inside `{{ }}` do?

choices.text: `minutes = 0`, to reset a field before showing it
choices.why: Assignment is only allowed in an event binding.

choices.text: `console.log(minutes)`, to debug
choices.why: A template sees the component and nothing else, so no globals.

choices.text: `course.sessions * minutes`
choices.why: Right. Reading properties and doing arithmetic are allowed.

choices.text: `new Date()`, to show today
choices.why: `new` is not allowed in a template expression.

prompt: Why are the bench's fields declared `protected`?

choices.text: The template reads them, code outside the class does not
choices.why: Right. That is exactly the access a template needs.

choices.text: A template can only read fields that are `protected`
choices.why: It can read `public` ones too; `protected` is the narrower choice that still works.

choices.text: `protected` makes them read-only
choices.why: That is `readonly`, a different word.

choices.text: So the CLI does not overwrite them on the next `ng generate`
choices.why: The CLI never edits an existing component's fields.

prompt: `{{ nothing?.name ?? 'no name' }}` printed `no name`. The operator that stopped at `null` instead of throwing is written ___.
`--html` showed no `value` attribute on the `<input>`, yet the field showed 45. Why?

choices.text: The binding failed, and the 45 is the browser's default
choices.why: A number field has no default of 45; the binding set it.

choices.text: `[value]` set the property, which does not reflect into the attribute
choices.why: Right. The attribute is only the starting text; the property is what is in the box.

choices.text: `look --html` removes attributes Angular added
choices.why: It removes only `_ngcontent-` and `_nghost-`, and the min and max were shown.

choices.text: Angular stores the value in a hidden attribute
choices.why: Nothing is hidden; it sets the DOM property.

prompt: `<td [colspan]="2">` failed with `NG8002: Can't bind to 'colspan' since it isn't a known property of 'td'`. Which fix keeps the binding?

choices.text: Import `CommonModule`, which teaches Angular table properties
choices.why: No module adds DOM properties; the property is called something else.

choices.text: Write `colspan="{{ 2 }}"`
choices.why: Interpolation in an attribute is a property binding too, and fails the same way.

choices.text: `[attr.colspan]="2"`
choices.why: Right. It sets the attribute by its HTML name.

choices.text: Add `CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA` to the component
choices.why: That silences checks for unknown elements; it would hide the mistake, not fix it.

prompt: Why `[disabled]="minutes >= 240"` rather than writing `disabled="false"` in the HTML when the button should be enabled?

choices.text: `disabled="false"` would be a build error
choices.why: It compiles; it just does not do what it says.

choices.text: In HTML its mere presence switches the control off
choices.why: Right. The binding passes a real boolean to the property.

choices.text: The property binding is faster to draw
choices.why: Speed is not the difference; meaning is.

choices.text: Buttons ignore attributes and only read properties
choices.why: They read both; the attribute's presence is what disables.

prompt: At 45 minutes, `[style.color]="minutes > 200 ? 'red' : null"` produced what on the paragraph?

choices.text: `style="color: null"`
choices.why: `null` removes the style rather than writing it.

choices.text: `style=""`, an empty attribute
choices.why: There was no `style` attribute at all.

choices.text: No `style` attribute at all
choices.why: Right. `null` means no value for that style.

choices.text: `style="color: black"`, the default
choices.why: Angular writes no default; it removes the style.

prompt: `[style.width.%]="minutes / 2.4"` with `minutes` at 45. What percentage did the bar's width get?
The lesson says to prefer a class to a style. Which case earns a style binding?

choices.text: Making overdue sessions red
choices.why: That is a state, `overdue`, and belongs in a class the stylesheet defines.

choices.text: A bar whose width follows a number
choices.why: Right. A continuous value has no class to name it.

choices.text: Hiding an element when a list is empty
choices.why: That is a state too; lesson 5's `@if` is the better tool.

choices.text: Bold text for long sessions
choices.why: The bench did exactly this with a class.

prompt: In `(input)="typed($event)"`, what is `$event`?

choices.text: The new value of the field, as a number
choices.why: It is the whole event; the method reads the value from its target.

choices.text: A copy of the component, so the method can change it
choices.why: The method already has the component as `this`.

choices.text: The DOM's own `Event` object
choices.why: Right. Hence `event.target as HTMLInputElement` to read the value.

choices.text: An Angular wrapper that only exists in development mode
choices.why: It is the browser's event, in every build.

prompt: `#note` on an input, then `(keydown.enter)="saved = note.value"`. What is `note` in that statement?

choices.text: The `<input>` element itself
choices.why: Right. A template reference variable names the element for the rest of the template.

choices.text: A field of the class, created by the `#`
choices.why: Nothing is added to the class; the name exists only in the template.

choices.text: The text typed so far, kept up to date by Angular
choices.why: It is the element; `.value` reads the text at that moment.

choices.text: The last key pressed
choices.why: Keys are what `$event` would carry, not `note`.

prompt: A designer asks for a clickable `<div>` that adds 15 minutes. Why does the lesson say to make it a `<button>`?

choices.text: `(click)` only works on buttons, so a div would never fire
choices.why: `(click)` works on any element; that is part of the problem.

choices.text: A `<div>` cannot hold text, only other elements
choices.why: It can hold anything.

choices.text: Buttons are faster to draw
choices.why: Drawing speed is not the reason.

choices.text: A `<div>` gets no Tab, no Enter and no name
choices.why: Right. `look` and a screen reader both found the controls by role and name.

prompt: Put what happened, when `look` clicked `Add 15` once, in order.
items: Angular drew the template again, showing 60

prompt: The broken bench template had three mistakes. How many did `ng build` report?

choices.text: Three, one per mistake
choices.why: The string handed to `[max]` was not reported.

choices.text: Two: the misspelt field and the missing argument
choices.why: Right. Bindings to plain HTML elements' properties are not type-checked.

choices.text: One, because the build stops at the first error
choices.why: The build lists every error it finds.

choices.text: None; templates are only checked by `ng test`
choices.why: `ng build` reported two.

prompt: Match each error code with the mistake that produced it in this lesson.

pairs.right: a field name with a typo
a method called without its argument
a binding to a property the element does not have
a tag no import made known

right_distractors: a string where a DOM property wants a number

prompt: Your template compiles with `strictTemplates` on. What can you conclude?

choices.text: The page shows the right numbers
choices.why: Compiling says nothing about whether the values are correct; tests do.

choices.text: Every binding to every element has the right type
choices.why: Bindings to plain HTML elements' properties are not checked.

choices.text: Every name exists and every call fits
choices.why: Right. That is what the compiler can promise.

choices.text: No user can make it throw an error
choices.why: Data at run time can still be wrong in ways types do not see.

prompt: `look --a11y main` first answered that nothing matched `main`. What did that reveal about the page?

choices.text: That `look` cannot read landmarks
choices.why: It read one as soon as it existed.

choices.text: That Angular removes `<main>` from templates
choices.why: There was no `<main>` in the template yet.

choices.text: It had no landmark for a screen reader to jump to
choices.why: Right. Wrapping the week in `<main>` gave it one.

choices.text: That the dev server was not running
choices.why: The same command found `main` once it was added.

prompt: What value did the accessibility tree give the progress bar named `Done this week`?
Where did the progress bar's name, `Done this week`, come from?

choices.text: An `aria-label` Angular adds to every `<progress>`
choices.why: Angular adds no labels; the template has to supply one.

choices.text: The `<label for="week-progress">` beside it
choices.why: Right. A progress bar is a labelable element, as a field is.

choices.text: The paragraph above it, which mentions the numbers
choices.why: Being nearby names nothing; the `for` attribute does.

choices.text: The `[max]` binding, which carries a description
choices.why: `[max]` sets the maximum and nothing else.

prompt: Which binding sends data from the DOM into the class?

choices.text: `[value]="minutes"`
choices.why: Square brackets carry data from the class to the DOM.

choices.text: `{{ minutes }}`
choices.why: Interpolation is one way too, class to page.

choices.text: `[class.long]="minutes > 40"`
choices.why: A class binding is a property binding, class to DOM.

choices.text: `(input)="typed($event)"`
choices.why: Right. Round brackets bring the event, and its data, back into the class.

prompt: Which of these are allowed in an event binding but not inside `{{ }}`? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: `minutes = 0`
choices.why: Right. Assignment is the event binding's exception.

choices.text: `saved = note.value`
choices.why: Right. An assignment too, reading a template reference.

choices.text: `course.sessions * minutes`
choices.why: Arithmetic is allowed in both.

choices.text: `hours(minutes)`
choices.why: Calling a method is allowed in both.
